name: push: a sum said aloud with what it comes to must add up: "8 plus 3 ... so k is 12" is caught, in digits or in words; a right sum, a sum with no total, and a letter's term ("7m minus 2") are left alone

lines: Say you have k minus 3 equals 8. Adding 3 to both sides gives k equals 8 plus 3. So k is 12. The 3 was subtracted on the left, so it shows up added on the right; check whether your 6 did the same.
Take y minus 4 equals 9. To clear the minus 4 you add 4 to both sides. So y equals 9 plus 4, which is 13. Now compare what happened to the 4 there with what you did to the 6 on your line.
Picture n minus 9 equals 10: you add 9 to both sides. So n equals 10 plus 9, which is 19. Do your 6 the same way on that line, then work out x and check it in the original equation yourself.
Picture 7m minus 2 equals 3m plus 9. Adding 2 to each side leaves 7m minus 3m equals 9 plus 2. The 2 lands on the right as a plus, so hold your six up against that.
Picture 4m minus 8 equals 3m plus 2. Adding 8 to both sides leaves m equals 2 plus 8. So m is 10.
Start from 5 minus 8, which is minus 3.
Moving the 6 over leaves 5 plus 6 on the right. Your line is 2 short of that.
